memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Fear the Lord your God, serve him only and take your oaths in his name. Do not follow other gods, the gods of the peoples around you; for the Lord your God, who is among you, is a jealous God and his anger will burn against you, and he will destroy you from the face of the land. - Deut 6:13-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Israel prepared to live among nations who worshipped many gods, God gave a firm command: fear Me, serve Me only, and do not follow the gods around you. The pull toward other gods would be constant — through neighbours, marriages, culture, and convenience. So God spoke plainly. He is a "jealous God," not with petty envy, but with the rightful jealousy of one who has entered a covenant of love and will not share His people's hearts with rivals.

The warning is sobering. Turning to other gods was not a minor slip but covenant betrayal, and it carried serious consequences. This reflects how seriously God takes idolatry — because idols are not harmless. They enslave, deceive, and lead people away from the only One who gives life. God's warning here flows from love, not cruelty; He wants to protect His people from the ruin that comes from forsaking Him.

We may not bow to carved images, but the temptation to serve rival "gods" is as real as ever — money, success, pleasure, approval, security. Anything that claims the loyalty owed to God alone has become an idol. Jesus was clear: "No one can serve two masters" (Matt 6:24). The good news is that in Christ we are freed from the tyranny of idols to serve the living God with joy. Let Him hold the throne of your heart, undivided and alone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What rival "gods" tempt me to divide my loyalty away from the Lord?
- Do I take God's call to serve Him alone seriously, or treat idolatry lightly?
- How does serving the living God free me compared to serving idols?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You alone are worthy of my worship and service. Expose the idols that quietly compete for my heart, and free me to serve You alone with joy. Let no rival share the throne that belongs to You. Amen.
